## Porsche Taycan
Landing Page Concept

Conceptual landing page for Porsche's Taycan EV, designed around emotional triggers, conversion rate optimization, and premium digital experience. A mobile-first Figma prototype with a multi-step pre-order flow.

Role: Designer
Brief: 3Pillar Global
Medium: Figma Prototype

Objective: Design a high-conversion landing page for the Taycan EV launch that communicates brand prestige while guiding visitors through an emotionally charged pre-order funnel. Every element, from typography to micro-copy, was crafted to trigger desire and reduce hesitation.

Hero & Visual Direction

Process

### From Brand Research to Prototype

The project began with deep immersion in Porsche's brand world: studying premium automotive landing pages, EV marketing campaigns, and conversion patterns in high-ticket ecommerce. A moodboard established the visual tension between raw performance and refined elegance.

Wireframes mapped the scroll narrative: hook → desire → specification → social proof → CTA. Each section answers an unspoken objection and moves the visitor forward. The pre-order flow was designed as a multi-step modal, using progressive disclosure to reduce cognitive load while maintaining momentum.

High-Fidelity Screens

The purchase decision is always to take advantage of timing. Every CTA should use emotional triggers and close quickly through a conversion trigger.

Prototype & Reflection

The final Figma prototype includes animated transitions between sections and a functional pre-order modal, demonstrating the full user journey from first impression to conversion. This concept brief sharpened my understanding of high-stakes landing page design, where brand prestige and conversion urgency have to coexist.

View Figma Prototype →

Design Decisions & Context

The competitive context shaped every decision: Tesla, Rivian, E-Tron, and Polestar were all positioning in the electric premium space. The focus had to be on making the Taycan feel irreplaceable, not just electric. The answer was visceral and behavioral design, targeting the sensory experience rather than specifications.

- Used the official Porsche press kit : high-fidelity images, brand guidelines, SVG logos, and licensed fonts

- One call-to-action per scroll section, so no competing messages and no decision fatigue

- One-page design for segmented digital marketing: invitation, email, social campaign, SMS, and QR code

- Multistep pre-order flow designed to reduce friction through progressive disclosure

- High-quality images with detail zoom across all 3 Taycan models

- Conversion via online chat for personalized, direct treatment (system modeled after existing Porsche programs in other countries)

- Color contrast treated for accessibility throughout

- SEO-ready: every button and CTA measurable by analytics tools, heat maps applicable from day one

## VIRTU4L — Brand, Website & AI-Powered VR Business · Dario Espinosa
URL: https://datadaeon.github.io/virtu4l.html
Summary: VIRTU4L — founding a VR entertainment business in Chiapas: brand identity, website, AI-powered operations, and physical VR center experience design.

personal business · founder

## VIRTU4L — Brand, Website
& AI-Powered VR Business

Founding and building Chiapas' first VR center from the ground up: complete brand identity , a multi-page website with an AI game assistant and online quoter, a digital marketing system, and an AI avatar that runs operations. Every touchpoint designed and built by hand.

context

01 — Overview

Personal Business · Founder

### The First VR Center in Chiapas

VIRTU4L is not a client project. It's a real business I co-founded, designed, and built in Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas. The challenge was not just design: it meant going from zero to a fully operational venue , with a brand, a digital presence, pricing strategy, marketing, and AI tooling all running simultaneously.

The venue features free-roaming Meta Quest headsets with 45+ VR titles in-room, Xbox Cloud Gaming, Gotcha (paintball), private events for birthdays, corporate team building, and concerts. As the experience lead, I handled everything from naming and visual identity to the code that powers the website, and kept iterating once the business was already running with customers walking in.

02 — Brand Identity

### Building from Zero: Logo, Palette & Voice

The name VIRTU4L (with the 4 standing in for the letter A) immediately signals the digital-first identity and sets it apart from generic venue names. The brand had to feel exciting and premium while staying accessible to families, teenagers, and corporates alike.

Brand Principle

Dark, immersive, neon-forward. The brand lives in the space between tech product and entertainment venue, more like a gaming company than a carnival. Red (#ef4444) as the primary action color; teal as the digital-future accent; black as the permanent foundation.

Color System

#EF4444
Primary action · CTA

#3CFFD0
Digital accent · highlights

#0A0A0F
Immersive background

Typography uses a clean bold sans across all touch points. Headers run heavy to create the cinematic weight the VR experience demands, while body copy stays readable across mobile and venue screens. The tag line "Experimenta la Realidad Virtual" is direct, action-first, and bilingual by design.

03 — Website Design & Development

Vibe-coded · Vanilla JS · No framework

### A Multi-Page Business Website Built from Scratch

The site was designed and developed end-to-end: no template, no CMS. Built in vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript with deliberate performance constraints: fast-loading on mobile, SEO-ready, and deployable without a backend.

/ index

Home

Hero, features, experience packages, games carousel, events, client logos, CTA

/ juegos

Games Catalog

45+ VR titles + 550+ Xbox Cloud with filter by genre, AI game mood assistant

/ cotizador

Quote Wizard

6-step interactive wizard: event type → package → location → extras → WhatsApp send

/ faq

FAQ

Accordion-based FAQ covering booking, safety, age limits, and accessibility

/ halloween

Seasonal Events

Themed landing for special events. Halloween 2024 was the first edition

interactive

AI Mood Assistant

JS-powered 2-step mood questionnaire that recommends up to 3 VR games

↑ Home page hero — full-bleed immersive layout with booking CTA above the fold

↑ Games catalog — filterable, searchable, 45+ VR titles

↑ Online quoter — 6-step wizard ending in a WhatsApp pre-filled message

Key Design Decision

The quote wizard was the single highest-impact UX feature. Instead of a generic contact form, users answer 6 structured questions (event type, package, extras, location) and get a WhatsApp message pre-filled with their configuration. Zero sales friction, zero back-and-forth.

04 — Business Development

### Pricing Architecture & Package Strategy

Defining the pricing model was as much a design challenge as a business one. The goal: make the entry point irresistible ($50 MXN walk-in), scale cleanly to group events, and never leave money on the table with vague "custom quotes".

Star

$50 MXN

5–10 min individual — gateway experience, walk-in, no booking needed

1 person · intro games only

Mini

$120 MXN

30 min individual — full catalog access, guided session

1 person · all games

Club ✦

$400 MXN

60 min group — private area, multiplayer, ideal for friends & family

2–4 people · most popular

Arena

$800 MXN

90 min events — full space, tournaments, competitions, corporate

5+ people · events & groups

Beyond walk-in packages, a parallel revenue track was designed for B2B and event rentals : birthday packages with Gotcha paintball add-ons, corporate team building with catering coordination, and venue rental for concerts and private events up to 50 people. Each has its own pricing logic and a dedicated section in the quote wizard.

Partnership

Gotcha Depredadores, a local paintball venue, was brought in as a strategic partner, expanding the offer to combined VR + Gotcha packages. This cross-sell drives higher AOV and differentiates VIRTU4L from a standard gaming lounge into a full entertainment destination .

05 — Digital Marketing & Social

### Content Strategy & AI-Assisted Execution

Running a business and creating daily content simultaneously is unsustainable without a system. VIRTU4L's social presence spans Instagram, TikTok, Threads, and Facebook. Each platform gets a distinct content format built around its own algorithm.

Instagram @virtu4lsc

Reels-first: in-venue gameplay clips, customer reactions, game highlights. High-production shorts drive reach; stories drive reservations via link-in-bio.

TikTok @realidadvirtu4l

Organic discovery channel: raw gameplay + funny moments format. Lower production cost, higher reach ceiling. Used for new game announcements and walk-in promotions.

AI-assisted content creation is central to the operation. Claude and Midjourney draft caption variants, social copy, and visual concepts, cutting content production time by 60% while keeping brand voice consistent. Seasonal campaigns (Halloween, summer breaks, corporate season) are planned and partially generated with AI.

Marketing Principle

The best marketing for a VR venue is showing people what it feels like to be inside one . All content strategy is anchored to first-person reaction content. The guest's face the moment they put on the headset is the most effective ad we can run.

06 — AI Tools Built

AI-native operations

### Three Distinct AI Systems for One Business

Running a small VR venue means wearing every hat. Rather than hiring for each gap, AI tools were designed and built to fill specific operational holes, each one scoped to a real pain point.

WEBSITE

AI Game Mood Assistant

Built into the games catalog page, a 2-step conversational filter asks the user how they feel today (tranquil / excited / social / first-timer / with kids) and recommends up to 3 VR titles matched to that mood and available session time. Pure vanilla JS, no API calls.

OPERATIONS

VOS — VIRTU4L Operations System

A Slack-native agent (Node.js + Ollama) handling daily checklists, reservations, sales tracking, and Dasha, an AI assistant that runs locally with zero cloud dependency. 293 passing tests. Full case study available separately.
→ VOS case study

BRAND

AI Avatar — Dasha

Created a branded AI avatar, Dasha, as the face of VIRTU4L's customer communications and operations assistant. Dasha has a defined personality (energetic, direct, local), appears in social content, and powers the Slack operations brain inside VOS. Designed with a consistent visual identity so the avatar becomes a recognizable character.

07 — Technical Stack

### Built to Run Without a Backend

Every decision in the technical stack was shaped by one constraint: this business runs on a tight budget in a city with limited dev talent. The stack had to be maintainable by me alone, fast to deploy, and free to host.

HTML5

CSS3

Vanilla JS

Google Calendar API

WhatsApp API

Google Maps embed

Netlify / GitHub Pages

Node.js (VOS)

Ollama (local LLM)

Claude (AI assist)

Midjourney (visuals)

No-backend design choice

The quote wizard generates a WhatsApp deep link with a pre-filled message constructed entirely in JS on the client side. The calendar booking uses Google's public calendar embed. There is no server, no database, no API keys exposed. Zero hosting cost, zero attack surface, zero maintenance overhead.

08 — Reflection

### What Running a Business Teaches a Designer

This project is ongoing. The business is live, customers are walking in, and the product keeps evolving. The difference between client work and founder work is that you feel every design decision in your bank account .

Learned: Speed beats perfect

The first version of the website launched in under 2 weeks. It was imperfect. It still generated the first 20 reservations. Every sprint since has been driven by real customer behavior, not assumptions.

Learned: AI amplifies solo founders

Running marketing, operations, development, and design simultaneously is only feasible because of AI tooling. Claude wrote first drafts of copy that I refined. Midjourney generated visual concepts in hours. VOS automated the operational checklist that used to require a dedicated person.

Ongoing challenge

Local market education is still a challenge: many potential customers in Tuxtla Gutiérrez have never tried VR. A significant part of the content strategy is converting curiosity into first-visit intent, not just retaining existing customers.

## VOS — VIRTU4L Operations System with Local AI · Dario Espinosa
URL: https://datadaeon.github.io/virtu4lslacksagent.html
Summary: Slack-native AI operations system for a VR venue. Daily checklists, reservations, sales tracking, and Dasha — a locally-hosted AI agent. 293 tests, 4 channels, 0 public URLs.

← back to work

Personal Project · Side Project

entertainment

## VOS — VIRTU4L
Operations System
with Local AI

A Slack-native operations brain for a real-world VR venue, built where the team already works. One operator can run a full day independently. The director keeps full visibility. Dasha , the AI assistant, handles what the team would otherwise forget.

How Might We

How might we give a solo VR venue operator full operational control, without building a custom admin panel, adding new logins, or switching tools during the workday?

The Problem

### Operations Running on WhatsApp and Memory

VIRTU4L is an independent VR entertainment venue in Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Chiapas. Sessions are short, guided, and high-turnover. One operator runs the floor: welcoming guests, managing headsets, processing sales, tracking reservations, and coordinating events.

Most small venues survive on a mix of WhatsApp groups, spreadsheets, and memory . That works until it doesn't: a double-booking, a missed opening checklist, an event nobody confirmed, a headset nobody cleaned. There was no single place to run the day, no visibility for the director, and no structured path for operators to grow.

// Pain · Operator

No structured workflow. Opening and closing tasks lived in a WhatsApp thread. Reservations were manual. Sales reconciliation happened at end of shift, if at all.

// Pain · Director

No real-time visibility. Had to ask the operator for updates instead of seeing them. Financial summaries required manual compilation. No pattern data, only anecdotes.

Visual Context · Slack Interface

### Dasha in Action

VOS meets the team inside Slack, the tool they already use. Each channel has a dedicated workflow. Below is a typical start-of-shift interaction in #operaciones-local .

# operaciones-local
VOS · Socket Mode · connected

Checklist apertura: completado 09:18 · cierre: pendiente

Message #operaciones-local

The Solution

### One Slack Layer, Four Dedicated Channels

VOS is not a website and not a mobile app. It is an operations layer inside Slack , built where the team already communicates. Bolt SDK Socket Mode means no public URL and no inbound ports; the bot initiates an outbound WebSocket to Slack and stays live on a Mac mini running pm2.

The architecture separates concerns by channel: operations, learning, marketing, and director oversight each get a dedicated agent with specific commands and guardrails. DashaGuard sits in front of every write operation, whether that's a calendar event, a sales record, or a financial action, enforcing double-booking checks, price tolerance windows, and director authentication on high-risk commands.

# operaciones-local

Daily checklist, reservaciones (Google Calendar), ventas (Loyverse POS), headset tracking, event setup, and gotcha coordination. One operator, one thread.

# overseer-director

Private director view. Financial dashboards, DashaGuard alerts, shift summaries, and two-factor authentication for sensitive writes. No operator access.

# formacion-ai

Career path Levels 1–5, Kanban-style task tracking, onboarding coaching, and daily learning nudges. Training is part of the workday, not a separate PDF.

# marketing-virtu4l

MKT-COACH advisory powered by Ollama. Content planning tied to real venue data: trending games, session signals, and seasonal context for Tuxtla Gutiérrez.

AI-Assisted Workflow

Solo build · Claude Code + Cursor

### Building VOS with Claude Code and Cursor

VOS was built solo, end to end, with AI as an active build partner rather than a code-completion tool. The interesting design work wasn't the Slack integration. It was deciding what Dasha is allowed to state as fact versus offer as a suggestion, and gating every write behind DashaGuard before it touches a real calendar, sale, or financial record.

VOS — AI-assisted process and tools by stage

Process

Drew the line between what Dasha can suggest versus what needs a verified fact or human sign-off
Live in production for the actual VR center team, on a real Mac mini

Key question
Where does this actually break today?
Why Slack, and what has to be gated before it ships?
Can one person actually ship this alone?
How does Dasha know the difference between a guess and a fact?
Does the team actually use it on a real shift?

← swipe to see every stage →

Architecture · D3

### System Architecture — VOS

Socket Mode means no reverse proxy, no public endpoint, no load balancer. The bot owns the connection. All external writes go through DashaGuard.check() before touching any service.

Key Decision

// design-decision

Why Slack and not a web panel? The team already lives in Slack. A custom admin panel means a new URL to bookmark, a new login to forget, and a screen nobody opens unless they're told to. VOS meets people where they work, with no onboarding friction and no context-switching mid-shift. The AI assistant feels like a colleague in the thread, not a form to fill out.

// design-decision

Local LLM (Ollama) over cloud API for advisory agents. Marketing coaching and career conversations don't need GPT-4. Ollama's gemma3:4b runs locally, so there's no per-token cost, no data leaving the machine, and no latency spike. For operational commands (checklist, sales, calendar) the bot uses deterministic business logic, not LLM inference, for reliability and auditability.

Reflection

"Building this entirely with Claude Code and Cursor showed me how fast a solo developer can move when the AI partner understands the domain. The hardest part wasn't the code. It was designing Dasha's behavioral rules so she never invents data and always knows the difference between a suggestion and a verified fact. Getting that boundary right is a design problem, not an engineering one."

## Walking Dog
App POC

Proof of concept for a dog-walking marketplace app called "Dog City." User research, business model validation, and UX design for a location-based service connecting dog owners with professional walkers.

Role: UX Designer
Type: POC · Marketplace
Model: Two-sided Platform

Objective: Validate a business model before committing to full product development. The POC combined market research, competitive analysis, and UX design to determine whether a dog-walking marketplace could achieve product-market fit, and how it should be designed to convert both dog owners and walkers.

Business Model

### Two-Sided Marketplace Dynamics

Dog City is a platform business: value is created by connecting two distinct user groups whose needs are complementary. The design had to serve both sides, building trust for owners and opportunity for walkers, without favoring one over the other.

#### Dog Owners

Need: reliable, trustworthy care for their pets on flexible schedules. Key friction: trust and real-time visibility

#### Dog Walkers

Need: consistent income and manageable client load. Key friction: discovery and booking efficiency

UX Design

In two-sided marketplace design, the first design decision is: which side bootstraps first? For Dog City, walkers are supply. Without them there is no product. The onboarding UX prioritized walker acquisition, then built owner trust on top of that foundation.

Reflection

The Walking Dog POC was an exercise in UX as business validation. It meant designing a business model through the lens of user behavior, not just designing screens. The research phase challenged initial assumptions about which features drive adoption on each side of the marketplace.

Location-based services add a critical trust dimension: users must feel safe before they will share location and payment data. The design solution embedded trust signals (verified profiles, real-time GPS tracking, rating systems) at every step of the journey rather than relegating them to a single "trust" section.

## From Identity to Shelf: Smartphone Brand & Packaging · Dario Espinosa
URL: https://datadaeon.github.io/yaiwa.html
Summary: Complete brand identity system and unboxing experience design for YAIWA smartphone by Spirit Asian Company. From name proposal to 3D packaging renders, extended to IBERIA and Spirit Credit Card.

// archive · older work

consumer-tech
Product Design
Industrial UX
Brand Identity
2017

## YAIWA
Smartphone Design

Full smartphone UI and industrial design concept for YAIWA, a Spirit Asia Company product. Visual identity, screen UI design, packaging direction, and product photography art direction.

Client: Spirit Asia Company
Role: Product Designer
Scope: Brand + UI + Packaging

Scope: End-to-end design responsibility for a hardware product entering a competitive mobile market. The work spanned from brand identity and visual language through to UI screen design and packaging: a full product design engagement requiring consistency across physical and digital touchpoints.

Brand & Identity

Product Design

UI & Packaging

Screen UI design followed the brand's visual language: clean, modern, and market-competitive. Packaging direction unified the physical product presentation with the digital experience identity.

Process & Extended Work

### From Name Proposal to Unboxing Experience

The original name was "Yawa." When expanding the market to the Americas, the team searched for a name with easy pronunciation across multiple languages. Spanish, English, and Portuguese speakers all needed to say it naturally. The final name became YAIWA .

- Complete brand identity system: visual language, color, typography, mark

- Packaging design: box structure and full unboxing experience design

- Digital content: screen wallpapers and 3D renders for both high-end and low-end smartphone SKUs

- Extended engagement: designs for IBERIA (Spanish Airlines) travel branding

- Spirit Credit Card travel account kit, smartphone-ready for use in 130+ countries

Tools: Adobe Dimension for 3D renders and photorealistic product visualization. The project started with a credit card identity for Spirit Asian Company and grew into a full smartphone brand system.

Reflection

YAIWA was an early and formative project in designing across the physical-digital boundary. Creating a consistent brand expression that worked equally on product hardware, retail packaging, and digital screens required a systems-first mindset, one that has informed all subsequent work in product and UX design.

Designing for an Asia-market client also pushed cultural adaptability: form factors, aesthetic preferences, and brand signaling all required contextual calibration beyond Western design defaults.

## Custom Plan, Zero Friction: Telecom UI Concept · Dario Espinosa

2021

## Zafyro
Mobile App UI

High-fidelity UI mockup for Zafyro, a mobile app concept. Focused on clean visual design, component consistency, and mobile-first interaction patterns. A visual showcase in systematic interface craft.

Role: UI/UX Designer
Medium: Figma
Type: Concept

Approach: This was an exercise in visual discipline: building a coherent, polished mobile UI from a concept brief. Every screen was crafted around component reusability, typographic hierarchy, and touch-target usability. The result is a high-fidelity mockup that communicates product vision with precision.

Concept & Approach

### Pay Only for the SIM You Actually Need

Zafyro was a service concept designed around a single insight: mobile plan pricing is opaque, bundled, and rarely matches actual usage. The product idea, "Create your plan, pay only for the SIM," let users configure exactly what they needed before activating anything.

- Mobile-first concept: the entire configuration experience was designed for thumb-reach interaction

- Plan builder UI: users select data, voice, and SMS amounts independently

- Payment tied only to SIM activation, with no commitment before the user was ready

- High-fidelity prototype demonstrated the full plan-creation-to-checkout journey

Visual Showcase

### High-Fidelity Mobile Interface

The Zafyro UI demonstrates a mature mobile design language: clean, structured, and purposeful. Component systems were built first, with screens assembled from consistent building blocks to ensure scalability across the product.

Reflection

### On Visual Systems

Zafyro was a compact but instructive project. The constraint of a single coherent visual identity across multiple screens pushed for disciplined design decision-making. Color, spacing, and type all follow strict rules that make the interface feel inevitable rather than arbitrary.

This kind of high-fidelity visual work informs how I approach larger UX systems: the visual layer is not decoration, it is communication.
